title: Magic Formula 1: if
lessonSummary: The first path is open! With if your code only acts when the condition is true.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: three simple if conditions.
Create level = 5. If level >= 5, print exactly: You are ready for the quest!

validation.expected: You are ready for the quest!

tasks.instruction: Create has_key = True. Use if (without a comparison) to print exactly: The door opens!

title: Comparison Operators
lessonSummary: Well judged! You know the comparison runes and the difference between = and ==.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: all comparison runes at work.
tasks.codeTemplate:
level = 15
if level == 15:
    print("✅ Correct: level is 15")

value = 10
print(f"Value: {value}")
print(f"{value} < 15: {value < 15}")
print(f"{value} <= 10: {value <= 10}")
print(f"{value} > 5: {value > 5}")
print(f"{value} >= 10: {value >= 10}")
print(f"{value} != 10: {value != 10}")

gold = 100
cost = 80
if gold > cost:
    print(f"🛍️ Purchase possible! Remaining: {gold - cost}")

tasks.instruction: Create level = 15. Use == in an if to print exactly: Correct: level is 15
Create value = 10 and print the result of the comparison with an f-string, exactly: 10 > 5: True
Create spell = "Fireball". Use != to print exactly: This is not a Frostbolt

title: Magic Formula 2: if-else
lessonSummary: Two paths, one decision! else catches everything the if did not.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: three if-else decisions.
Create roll = 8. If roll >= 15 print Critical hit!, otherwise print exactly: Normal strike
Create gold = 45 and cost = 50. If gold >= cost print Purchase successful!, otherwise print exactly the missing amount with an f-string: Not enough gold! Missing: 5

title: Magic Formula 3: if-elif-else
lessonSummary: Many paths, one winner! Python takes the first true path and skips the rest.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a level rating and an element spell.

Create xp = 750. Rate it with if-elif-else: xp >= 1000 prints Master!, xp >= 500 prints Advanced!, xp >= 100 prints Beginner!, otherwise Still much to learn... Your program must print exactly: Advanced!

Create element = "Air". Use if-elif-else with the four elements: Fire prints Fire Strike!, Water prints Water Torrent!, Air prints Wind Gust!, Earth prints Earthquake!, anything else prints Unknown element! Your program must print exactly: Wind Gust!

title: Magic Formula 4: Logical Operators
lessonSummary: Conditions combined! and, or and not let you build precise rules.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: and, or, not and a hero class.

title: Magic Formula 5: Nested Conditions
lessonSummary: Paths within paths! Every extra level needs one more level of indentation.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the locked door.

validation.expected: The key fits - the door opens!

tasks.instruction:
Create door_locked = True and right_key = False. Use a nested if so that your program prints exactly: This key does not fit.
The program should print The door is locked. first, then decide about the key. If the door is not locked it should print The door is already open.
Create door_locked = False and right_key = True. Use the same nested structure as before (locked door with key check, else already open). Your program must print exactly: The door is already open.
